title: Let close --allow-legacy-usage excuse recovered token-mismatch records
summary: Job 2fsa's producer invocation record exists only in the state directory, so close sees it as new and the legacy scope (byte-identical in the parent commit) does not excuse it. Extend the flag, and only the flag, to records that `athena close` itself recovers from the state directory, covering token as well as cost mismatches and printing each one. The audience is the maintainer running the close.

defaults_applied.how: New lifecycle and gate tests; cargo test, clippy and fmt --check pass.
Fix the legacy scope for recovered records generally, not a special case for the 2fsa job id.
Criteria run close with and without the flag and check the outcomes.
Decision record, changelog and help text written for outside readers.
One focused change to the flag's scope.
The limit of the excuse is enforced in gate code and tests, not prose.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The 2fsa producer invocation record is only in the state directory (confirmed by the user); only invocations/01-reader.json is committed.
Without the flag the gate rule is unchanged.
The excuse applies only to records athena close recovers itself, not to records altered or added by other means.
Each excused record is printed with its mismatch kind.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new lifecycle test creates an interrupted job whose state-directory invocation record has token counts that disagree with its models_used. `athena close --allow-legacy-usage` succeeds, prints a 'letting a legacy usage record through' line naming the token mismatch, and the closing outcome reconciles. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle`.
The same close without the flag is still refused with 'usage records reconcile', and the message names --allow-legacy-usage. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle`.

A gate test shows that under the legacy scope an invocation record that is new or altered outside close's own recovery still fails reconciliation, and a wrong outcome total is still refused. Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`.
`cargo test` passes, and `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

docs/decisions.md has a new decision or an amendment to D101 giving the case, the alternatives and the limit of the excuse. CHANGELOG.md and the close row in docs/design/athena-v0.md describe the wider coverage.
The flag's help text and doc comments in main.rs and manage.rs state exactly which records it excuses.

out_of_scope: Relaxing the reconciliation gate when the flag is absent
Changing the pricing or cost rules
